headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: Argo Workflows can pass artifacts to Marker, but Marker is local-only and has no filesystem write or network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can produce artifacts and Marker processes documents, so a manual or file-based bridge is plausible. However, Marker has no filesystem write, no MCP, and no browser/network egress, so the injection path is limited and not a default shared channel. The pair is safer than a permissive parser chain.
conditions: IF Argo outputs are manually copied into Marker inputs
IF a shared workspace or artifact handoff is introduced
mitigations: Use a dedicated handoff folder with read-only permissions
Strip instructions from upstream artifacts before ingestion
Require human review of any generated text before reuse
Disable any automation that forwards raw workflow output
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo Workflows can touch artifacts and parameters, but Marker has no filesystem read, no network egress, and no declared data classes. That makes unintended leakage from Marker unlikely; the main exposure is Argo-side artifact handling, not a bidirectional exfiltration path. The pair does not show shared credentials or a shared workspace.
conditions: IF sensitive artifacts are placed into Argo inputs
IF Marker is given those artifacts through an external wrapper
mitigations: Limit artifact contents to non-sensitive samples
Store sensitive inputs outside the workflow boundary
Review workflow logs for embedded data
Run Marker on redacted copies only
requires-engineering: enforce per-artifact access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows exposes REST/GRPC APIs and allowlisted egress, while Marker has no filesystem write, no git modification, and no network egress. There is no overlapping mutable surface in the profiles, so a write-write conflict is not plausible from the documented capabilities.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants Marker write access not shown in the profile
IF both agents are reconfigured to mutate the same directory
mitigations: Keep Marker in read-only mode
Avoid mounting shared writable volumes
Separate workflow state from document-processing outputs
Audit any wrapper that adds write permissions
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo Workflows can generate artifacts that Marker may transform into documents, so B can consume A's output as input. Because Marker is a document processor and no verification or provenance controls are shown, errors or hallucinated structure from Argo can cascade into downstream outputs in default use. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF Marker consumes Argo-produced artifacts without validation
IF downstream automation treats Marker output as authoritative
mitigations: Add a validation step between the agents
Compare Marker output against source artifacts
Require human approval before downstream use
Log provenance for each transformed document
requires-engineering: implement schema checks on handoff

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either profile. Argo touches artifacts and parameters, while Marker lists no data classes touched, so there is no evidenced compliance breach pathway specific to this pair.
conditions: IF future documentation shows regulated data classes flowing through both agents
IF one agent is deployed under stricter residency or retention rules
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents
Map retention settings before deployment
Restrict regulated data from the workflow
Review vendor compliance statements
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement at orchestration time
